full_target: Let n,m be positive integers, u:ℝ^n×(0,∞)→ℝ^m jointly smooth, and q∈ℝ^m have Euclidean norm one. Assume for all x∈ℝ^n and t>0, |u(x,t)|=1; for every (x,t) there exists a(x,t)∈ℝ with u_tt(x,t)−Δ_xu(x,t)=a(x,t)u(x,t), with no regularity of a assumed; and for every finite closed interval J⊂(0,∞) there exists compact C_J⊂ℝ^n such that u(x,t)=q for all x∉C_J and t∈J. Define e(x,t)=||u_t(x,t)||²+Σ_{j=1}^n||∂_{x_j}u(x,t)||² and E(t)=∫_{ℝ^n}e(x,t)dx using Lebesgue measure, Euclidean vector norms, and the Frobenius/Hilbert–Schmidt spatial-gradient square; Δ_x is the componentwise sum of second spatial derivatives. Prove e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable for every t>0, E is differentiable at every t>0, and E'(t)=0. No endpoint t=0 assertion is included.
conclusion: For every r>0, e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

hypotheses.statement: For all x,r>0 there exists a∈R with u_tt−Δ_xu=a u.
For each compact interval J⊂(0,∞), compact C_J exists with u=q outside C_J throughout J.

definitions.definition: For x∈ℝⁿ and r>0, e(x,r)=‖u_t(x,r)‖₂²+∑_{j=1}^n‖∂_{x_j}u(x,r)‖₂²; the vector norms are Euclidean, and the spatial-gradient term is the Frobenius/Hilbert–Schmidt square of the Jacobian.

definitions.type: partial function from positive reals to real numbers, defined only at times of integrability
definitions.definition: For r>0 such that e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E(r) is the finite real Lebesgue integral ∫ e(x,r) dx. This definition assigns no value at times for which integrability has not been established.

definitions.type: For smooth u:ℝⁿ×(0,∞)→ℝᵐ, a differential operator with Δ_xu:ℝⁿ×(0,∞)→ℝᵐ.
definitions.definition: For each (x,r), (Δ_xu)(x,r)=∑_{j=1}^n ∂²u(x,r)/∂x_j², with each second derivative taken componentwise in ℝᵐ.

definitions.type: positive integer k maps to Euclidean/Borel/Lebesgue measure space on ℝᵏ
definitions.definition: For each positive integer k, identify ℝᵏ with the finite product Fin k→ℝ, equip it with its Euclidean norm and topology, the Borel σ-algebra generated by that topology, and product Lebesgue measure (the product of one-dimensional Lebesgue volume on each coordinate).
